lecture_03.title: CS336 Spring 2026, Lecture 3: Everything you didn't want to know about LM architecture and hyperparameters
lecture_03.anchor_convention: lecture_03.pdf:p<page>, page numbers from `pdftotext -layout` form feeds (title slide = p1; 67 pages)
lecture_03.note: Evidence is the text layer of the slides (lecture_03.txt), extracted page-by-page by discover_slides.py. Most empirical results (pre/post-norm curves, Narang and Shazeer tables, Kaplan basin, aspect-ratio plots, weight-decay plots, perplexity hits of MQA) are figures without a text layer; where a KP relies on such a figure the filtering_note says so and the statement carries only what the slide text says. Stacked fractions (p14 RMSNorm formula, p38 8/3, p58-p61 arithmetic-intensity expressions) come out of pdftotext as scattered digits; the quotes reconstruct them from the layout and say so.

rope.title: Atlas paper thread: RoFormer (RoPE), Su et al. 2021
rope.note: Slides p31-p35 teach RoPE; those pages are covered by the rope thread (rope-position-goal, rope-2d-solution, rope-block-diagonal, rope-relative-position, rope-multiplicative-vs-additive, rope-per-layer-application). Referenced here via external_prerequisites only; the position-embedding KP in this thread covers the taxonomy on p30.

xiong_2020_prenorm.title: On Layer Normalization in the Transformer Architecture (Xiong et al., 2020)
xiong_2020_prenorm.note: Figures on p10, p11, p12 ('Figure from Xiong 2020'): pre-norm vs post-norm block diagram, training curves, and gradient-norm-per-layer (gradient attenuation) plots.

nguyen_salazar_2019.title: Transformers without Tears: Improving the Normalization of Self-Attention (Nguyen & Salazar, 2019)
nguyen_salazar_2019.note: Cited on p11 and p12 as 'Salazar and Ngyuen 2019' (author order and spelling as on the slides); figures for pre-norm training without warmup and gradient spikes.

rmsnorm_2019.title: Root Mean Square Layer Normalization (Zhang & Sennrich, 2019)
rmsnorm_2019.note: Not cited by name on the slides; p14 states the RMSNorm formula y = x / sqrt(mean(x^2) + eps) * gamma without attribution.

ivanov_data_movement.title: Data Movement Is All You Need: A Case Study on Optimizing Transformers (Ivanov et al., MLSys 2021)
ivanov_data_movement.note: Cited on p15 and p16 as 'Ivanov et al 2023' (the slide's year; the arXiv preprint is 2020, MLSys 2021). Source of the FLOPs-vs-runtime breakdown figure where normalization is a small share of FLOPs but a visible share of runtime.

narang_2021_modifications.title: Do Transformer Modifications Transfer Across Implementations and Applications? (Narang et al., 2021)
narang_2021_modifications.note: Cited as 'Narang et al 2020' on p17 (RMSNorm speed and quality) and p25 (gated activations). Tables are figures on the slides.

shazeer_2020_glu.title: GLU Variants Improve Transformer (Shazeer, 2020)
shazeer_2020_glu.note: p24 'Shazeer 2020': table of GLU variants vs ReLU/GeLU on T5 pretraining; also the origin of the 2/3 scaling of d_ff for gated layers (slide p23 states the 2/3 without citation).

kaplan_2020_scaling.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models (Kaplan et al., 2020)
kaplan_2020_scaling.note: p40 ('[Kaplan+ 2020]') shows the d_ff/d_model basin figure; p46 shows the aspect-ratio figure. Numbers on those slides are only in figures except the '1-10' basin on p40.

raffel_2020_t5.title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer (Raffel et al., 2020)
raffel_2020_t5.note: p39: T5 11B d_ff = 65,536 with d_model = 1024 ('64-times multiplier'), and p43/p44 head and aspect-ratio rows for T5 and T5 v1.1.

tay_2021_scale_efficiently.title: Scale Efficiently: Insights from Pre-training and Fine-tuning Transformers (Tay et al., 2021)
tay_2021_scale_efficiently.note: p45 and p46 ('[Tay et al 2021]'): depth vs width figures; the slide's claim that very deep models are harder to parallelize and have higher latency.

andriushchenko_2023_wd.title: Why Do We Need Weight Decay in Modern Deep Learning? (Andriushchenko et al., 2023)
andriushchenko_2023_wd.note: p50: weight decay in LLMs is not about overfitting; it interacts with the (cosine) learning-rate schedule. Supporting plots are figures only.

devlin_2014_zloss.title: Fast and Robust Neural Network Joint Models for Statistical Machine Translation (Devlin et al., ACL 2014)
devlin_2014_zloss.note: p54 '[From Devlin 2014]': the self-normalization penalty on log Z that PaLM later called the z-loss. The formula on p54 is an image; the slide text has no coefficient.

palm_2022.title: PaLM: Scaling Language Modeling with Pathways (Chowdhery et al., 2022)
palm_2022.note: Named on the slides for parallel layers (p28), d_ff ratio 4 under SwiGLU (p38), head dim 258 (p43, as printed), vocab 256000 (p47), z-loss (p54). Not cited by paper on the slides, only by model name.

dehghani_2023_vit22b.title: Scaling Vision Transformers to 22 Billion Parameters (Dehghani et al., 2023)
dehghani_2023_vit22b.note: p55 '[Dehgani 2023, Idefcs, Chameleon]' (spelling as on the slide): QK-norm originated in vision and multimodal models.

gemma2_2024.title: Gemma 2: Improving Open Language Models at a Practical Size (Gemma Team, 2024)
gemma2_2024.note: Logit soft-capping via tanh (p56) is the Gemma 2 recipe; the slide names no paper and gives no cap value in text.

shazeer_2019_mqa.title: Fast Transformer Decoding: One Write-Head is All You Need (Shazeer, 2019)
shazeer_2019_mqa.note: p61 (MQA idea) and p63 'Small PPL hit w/ MQA [Shazeer 2019]'; the incremental arithmetic-intensity argument on p58-p61 follows this paper's analysis.

ainslie_2023_gqa.title: GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints (Ainslie et al., 2023)
ainslie_2023_gqa.note: p62-p63: grouped-query attention, 'Low/no hit w/ GQA [Ainslie 2023]' (table is a figure).

child_2019_sparse.title: Generating Long Sequences with Sparse Transformers (Child et al., 2019)
child_2019_sparse.note: p64 '[Child et al 2019]': sparse / strided attention pattern figure.

kv_cache_blog.title: Transformers KV Caching Explained (João Lages, Medium)
kv_cache_blog.note: p59: animation of the KV cache (image on the slide).

fireworks_mqa_blog.title: Multi-Query Attention is All You Need (Fireworks AI blog)
fireworks_mqa_blog.note: p61 figure of MQA vs MHA head layout.

grootendorst_gemma4.title: A Visual Guide to Gemma 4 (Maarten Grootendorst newsletter)
grootendorst_gemma4.note: p66: diagrams of interleaved local/global attention in Gemma 4, OLMo 3, Qwen 3.5.
